title: sales.refund — payload
description: Refunds a COMPLETED sale by ELIGIBLE TENDER, with an EDITABLE split (ADR-0386 decision 3). The operator decides how much goes back to each leg of the original payment; the proportional split is the screen's default proposal, not a cage. Two independent axes: `payment_id` is where the money comes FROM (capped at what that leg was charged minus what it already gave back — going over is refused naming which leg), and the optional `to_payment_method_id` is where it goes TO (defaults to the leg's own method; needed when that method is no longer available, which is the case Square never solved). Unlike sales.void, an invoiced sale CAN be refunded: the refund is the economic fact and the credit note is its document.

reason.description: Why the money goes back: shown in the sale's history and carried in sale.refunded.

idempotency_key.description: One per refund ATTEMPT. A retry with the same key writes nothing and answers with the SAME refund id — which is the stable refund_ref services needs to give a voucher session back.

allocations.description: How much goes back to each tender. Legs not named here get nothing.

payment_id.description: The leg of the original payment (sales.payments) whose money comes back.

amount.description: Cents (ADR-0123). Never more than that leg's `remaining` in sales.refund_options.

to_payment_method_id.description: Where the money physically goes. Omit to return it the way it was charged; name another method when the original one is no longer available.

lines.description: services#158 — the lines of the sale that go back with this money. Optional: omitted or empty, only money goes back. Each line is recorded once (sales.refund_lines) and announced in sale.refunded.lines, so the module that sold it reacts to THAT line (services voids the voucher sold on it). A line that is not of this sale, named twice, or already returned by an earlier refund is refused.
